parsed.attack: Their own kill line sets the acceptance bar at 5 referrals per 100 buyers over six months - a coefficient of 0.05 on a six-month cycle, an order of magnitude below the 0.3-0.7 a healthy loop needs, and it is written as a pass condition rather than a failure. The referrer's incentive is also absent: JATC and college instructors teach a mandated curriculum and are already bound to Mike Holt or NEC handbook materials that they or the programme sell, and a journeyman gains nothing by naming a $29 app to an apprentice he is already supervising for free. Then the loop's own fuel burns off - the buyer passes the licensing exam and exits the population permanently, so the base is fully replaced every year with no retained advocates and no recurring revenue to fund a spiff.
parsed.strongest_defence: The jurisdiction binding is what gives the instructor a reason to speak: no generic flashcard app matches this state's current code cycle, so naming it is useful rather than promotional, and apprentices concentrate in r/electricians, trade-school cohorts and trade TikTok where 'conduit fill, eight weeks to my exam' is a free, extremely high-intent search.
parsed.verdict_reason: The plan's own referral target is a coefficient of 0.05 on a six-month cycle against an annually replaced user base, which is a trickle rather than a loop.
